note: Art direction for Aluxes (AL1), since 2026-09-27: an ancient Maya wall painting, after the owner's references (Maya murals: flat mineral colours on weathered lime plaster, bold red-brown outlines). An alux is never drawn as a person: he is a tiny living clay figurine (the healer shapes aluxes from clay), knee-high, with a doll-like clay face, round hollow eyes with a spark of light, corn-husk hat and wrap, painted a little faint because aluxes are usually invisible. The first mural drafts drew aluxes as small Maya villagers; the owner rejected that as portraying real people as spirits. Drawn with tools/generate_art.py --reference <the owner's mural image>.
style: A painting for a collectible card game that looks like a photograph of a real ancient Maya wall painting, in exactly the art style of the reference image and of the murals of Calakmul, Bonampak and San Bartolo. Bold, confident brush outlines in dark red-brown and black; flat fills of mineral pigment: dominant red-orange and terracotta, ochre yellow, cream, soft black, and small touches of Maya blue and jade green. Textiles and surfaces are decorated the Maya way, with rows of black dots, U-shaped marks, stripes and fringed hems. Figures are drawn as the Maya drew people: in profile, with the typical Maya face (sloping forehead, long nose, almond eye), elegant expressive hands, flat, with no modern perspective, no shading, no 3D, no cartoon style and NOT a modern children's-book illustration. The wall is old: pale lime plaster with a rough chalky texture, faded and flaking paint, a few small white patches where the plaster has fallen away, stains and hairline cracks, so the scene feels a thousand years old. IMPORTANT: the reference shows ancient Maya nobles at a feast. Use ONLY its art style, texture and palette. Do NOT copy its figures or scene, and do NOT draw gods, kings, rulers' headdresses, idols or temples. The subject is always an alux, a spirit of the Maya cornfield, and an alux is NEVER drawn as a person, a child, a villager or a Maya man: he is a tiny living clay figurine only knee-high to a person (corn stalks tower over him, an ear of corn is as long as his whole arm), shaped from smooth terracotta clay like the little clay figures a Maya healer makes and brings to life: a big round head, a round belly, short stubby arms and legs, clay-coloured skin with fingerprints and a few fine cracks, two round hollow eyes each holding a tiny spark of light, and a small smiling mouth: a doll-like clay face, NOT a human face, and no hair. He wears only a little hat folded from a green corn husk and a wrap of twisted corn husks around his waist. Because aluxes are usually invisible, his outline is painted a little faint, with the plaster showing through him slightly. Gentle, a little mischievous, never scary. People appear only where a card asks for one, and then they are ordinary full-size villagers, never tiny. One clear main subject, fully in frame. Absolutely no glyphs, hieroglyph blocks, writing, letters, numbers, symbols, logos, borders, card frames or watermarks.

subjects.AL1-H01-kitten: the most endearing alux of all, the smallest and roundest, a tiny living clay figurine only knee-high to a person (corn stalks tower over him, an ear of corn is as long as his whole arm), shaped from smooth terracotta clay like the little clay figures a Maya healer makes and brings to life: a big round head, a round belly, short stubby arms and legs, clay-coloured skin with fingerprints and a few fine cracks, two round hollow eyes each holding a tiny spark of light, and a small smiling mouth: a doll-like clay face, NOT a human face, and no hair. He wears only a little hat folded from a green corn husk and a wrap of twisted corn husks around his waist. Because aluxes are usually invisible, his outline is painted a little faint, with the plaster showing through him slightly, his corn-husk hat a size too big for him and one little red bead on his wrap. Not a god, not a king, no headdress, no crown. He sits in the doorway of his doll-sized house of pale stone with a little palm-thatch roof at the edge of the cornfield, hugging a golden ear of corn bigger than himself, a small spotted dog curled up beside him. Tender and cosy.

banner: The edge of a Maya cornfield in Yucatán beside the forest: tall green-and-ochre corn plants in rows, a great ceiba tree, and at the field's edge a tiny house no bigger than a shoebox, built of stone with a little palm-thatch roof and a dark doorway, the alux's house. In front of it, offerings on the ground: a gourd bowl of corn drink, a small cup of honey and a few cacao beans. Rain clouds gather over the forest.
